classification.difficultyReason: After finding the altitude with tangent, infer an unlabelled angle in the second triangle from both right-angle marks and complementary angles, then identify the new opposite and adjacent sides. The shared height is prompted, but the angle connection is not.

content.prompt: For the diagram on the right:

spec.description: Right triangle BAD with altitude AC to horizontal BD; right-angle marks at A and C.
spec.mathematics: BC=15 cm, angle ABC=37 degrees, AC=h cm, CD=x cm. Coordinates derive from the supplied angle and perpendicular relationships.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the value of $h$, correct to 2 decimal places.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use this value to find $x$, correct to 2 decimal places.

answer.short:
$x=8.52\text{ cm}$

Use the shared height and the complementary angle in the second right triangle.
answer.worked:
$\angle BAC=90^\circ-37^\circ=53^\circ$, so $\angle CAD=90^\circ-53^\circ=37^\circ$.
Using the unrounded value of $h$ in $\triangle ACD$:
$$\begin{align*}\tan37^\circ&=\frac{x}{h}\\x&=h\tan37^\circ\\x&=15\tan37^\circ\tan37^\circ\\x&\approx8.52\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
